main_text.p: Deo coronari audaciam in resistendo; sed in ferendo patientiam. Epistola prior Vincentio scripta ita se habet: [{y}terror temporalium Potestatum, quando veritatem oppugnant iustis, fortibus, gloriosa probatio est, infirmis periculosa tentatio: non est tamen Potestas nisi a Deo, qui autem resistit Potestati, Dei ordinationi resistit. Vis autem non timere potestatem? bonum fac, & habebis laudem ex illa. Sive enim Potestas veritati favens aliquem corrigat, laudem habet ex illa qui fuerit emendatus, sive inimica veritati in aliquem saeviat, laudem habet ex illa qui victor fuerit coronatus.] z 166. Posterior Epistola Donatistis directa (qui nimis procaciter & petulanter Majestatem Imperatoriam coticulcabant,) ita priori suffragatur: [Imperatores si in errore essent (quod absit) pro errore suo contra veritatem Leges darent, per quas iusti & probarentur & coronarentur?] Non dicit ad arma confugerent & coronarentur, nec a iuramento fidelitatis deficerent & coronarentur: sed probaretur eorum constantia, & coronaretur patientia.

page.notes: Left page: "y" is the reference mark in the text and in the margin note "Epist.48." (the note reads "y Epist.48." on the scan). The margin mark beside "166." is printed as an x-like glyph; I read it as z, matching the text mark, so it is uncertain: [?]. The mark "z" in the text before "Posterior" is also a possible misreading. Long s is printed in the scan and is rendered here as plain s. The right page is cropped at the right edge: only the first letters of its lines are visible, so those fragments are incomplete and their readings are uncertain. Its page number and running head are not visible. No catchword, signature or page-foot furniture is visible.
